refs.quote: Dantrium Intravenous is indicated, along with appropriate supportive measures, for the management of the fulminant hypermetabolism of skeletal muscle characteristic of malignant hyperthermia crises in patients of all ages.

Dantrium Intravenous should be administered by continuous rapid intravenous push beginning at a minimum dose of 1 mg/kg, and continuing until symptoms subside or the maximum cumulative dose of 10 mg/kg has been reached.

dose.frequency: continuous rapid IV push until symptoms subside (maximum cumulative 10 mg/kg)

regimens.dose_text: Discontinue all anesthetic agents and administer 100% oxygen. Administer by continuous rapid IV push beginning at a minimum dose of 1 mg/kg, continuing until symptoms subside or maximum cumulative dose of 10 mg/kg is reached. May repeat regimen if physiologic and metabolic abnormalities reappear. Reconstitute each 20 mg vial with 60 mL sterile water for injection USP (without bacteriostatic agent).

refs.quote: Pediatric Dose: Experience to date indicates that the dose of Dantrium Intravenous for pediatric patients is the same as for adults.

refs.quote: Dantrium Intravenous is also indicated preoperatively, and sometimes postoperatively, to prevent or attenuate the development of clinical and laboratory signs of malignant hyperthermia in individuals judged to be malignant hyperthermia susceptible.
The recommended prophylactic dose of Dantrium Intravenous is 2.5 mg/kg, starting approximately 1-1/4 hours before anticipated anesthesia and infused over approximately 1 hour.

dose.frequency: single IV infusion over ~1 hour starting ~1.25 hours before anesthesia

regimens.dose_text: 2.5 mg/kg IV starting approximately 1-1/4 hours before anticipated anesthesia and infused over approximately 1 hour. Additional individualized IV doses may be indicated during anesthesia/surgery if early clinical or blood gas signs appear or for prolonged surgery.

refs.quote: Oral Administration of Dantrium Capsules: Administer 4 to 8 mg/kg/day of oral Dantrium Capsules in three or four divided doses for 1 or 2 days prior to surgery, with the last dose being given with a minimum of water approximately 3 to 4 hours before scheduled surgery.

dose.frequency: 4 to 8 mg/kg/day in 3 or 4 divided doses for 1 to 2 days prior to surgery

regimens.dose_text: 4 to 8 mg/kg/day orally in 3 or 4 divided doses for 1 or 2 days prior to surgery, with the last dose given with a minimum of water approximately 3 to 4 hours before scheduled surgery. Adjust within range to avoid weakness, drowsiness, or GI irritation.

regimens.indication: Malignant Hyperthermia Post-Crisis Follow-Up (Recurrence Prevention) — Oral Capsules

refs.quote: Post Crisis Follow-Up: Dantrium Capsules , 4 to 8 mg/kg/day, in four divided doses should be administered for 1 to 3 days following a malignant hyperthermia crisis to prevent recurrence of the manifestations of malignant hyperthermia.

dose.frequency: 4 to 8 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses for 1 to 3 days post-crisis

regimens.dose_text: 4 to 8 mg/kg/day orally in 4 divided doses for 1 to 3 days following a malignant hyperthermia crisis to prevent recurrence.

regimens.indication: Malignant Hyperthermia Postoperative Recurrence Prevention (When Oral Not Practical)

refs.quote: Dantrium Intravenous may be used postoperatively to prevent or attenuate the recurrence of signs of malignant hyperthermia when oral administration of Dantrium Capsules is not practical. The dose of Dantrium Intravenous in the postoperative period must be individualized, starting with 1 mg/kg or more as the clinical situation dictates.

dose.frequency: individualized postoperatively starting at 1 mg/kg or more

regimens.dose_text: Individualized IV dosing starting with 1 mg/kg or more as the clinical situation dictates when oral administration is not practical postoperatively.

tier.note: Pregnancy Category C: no adequate and well-controlled human studies, and animal studies show embryocidal effects/decreased pup survival at 7x human oral dose; use during pregnancy only if potential benefit justifies fetal risk.

refs.quote: Pregnancy: Pregnancy Category C: Dantrium has been shown to be embryocidal in the rabbit and has been shown to decrease pup survival in the rat when given at doses seven times the human oral dose. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Dantrium Intravenous should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.

pregnancy_pk.value: Readily crosses the placenta with maternal and fetal whole blood levels approximately equal at delivery; neonatal levels fall ~50% per day for 2 days before declining sharply.

refs.quote: Dantrolene readily crossed the placenta, with maternal and fetal whole blood levels approximately equal at delivery; neonatal levels then fell approximately 50% per day for 2 days before declining sharply.

lactation_summary.value: Detected in human milk at low concentrations (<2 mcg/mL) during repeat IV administration; decide whether to discontinue nursing or drug based on maternal importance.

refs.quote: Dantrolene has been detected in human milk at low concentrations (less than 2 micrograms per mL) during repeat intravenous administration over 3 days. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants from dantrolene, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or to discontinue the drug, taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother.

value.management: Monitor neuromuscular transmission with a peripheral nerve stimulator and adjust relaxant doses cautiously.
